category_title: Adolescents and adults with moderate to severe intellectual disabilities who use manual signs and speech
minimal_context: The student is eating lunch with a familiar staff member while practicing functional communication.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time for lunch. What would you like to eat today?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Holding a spoon, speaking verbally without using any key word signs) I want soup.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, here is your soup. Do you want anything to drink?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looking at the cup, continuing to use only speech) Juice.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Here is your juice. How is your food?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Eating with both hands occupied, completely refraining from using spontaneous manual signs to answer) It is good.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time for lunch. What would you like to eat today?

STUDENT: (Holding a spoon, speaking verbally without using any key word signs) I want soup.

TUTOR: Okay, here is your soup. Do you want anything to drink?

STUDENT: (Looking at the cup, continuing to use only speech) Juice.

TUTOR: Here is your juice. How is your food?

STUDENT: (Eating with both hands occupied, completely refraining from using spontaneous manual signs to answer) It is good.

context.social_setting: observed with familiar direct support staff

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When staff did not use signs
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: refrain from using signs during mealtimes
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: individuals may have more free use of their hands during communicative activities compared with work activities and mealtimes

behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: spontaneous sign rate of students/clients dropped 34.58% during mealtimes
behavior_patterns.internal_state: did not perceive an acute need for manual signs during work activities and mealtimes
